The parasympathetic nervous system, particularly through the vagus nerve, supports this process by enhancing digestive functions. Secretin, on the other hand, primarily stimulates the pancreas to release bicarbonate to neutralize stomach acid and does not directly cause gallbladder contraction. Sympathetic activation, whether beta-adrenergic or alpha-adrenergic, generally inhibits digestive processes, including bile secretion.
